analysis:
Reviewed ClusterService.swift: base 912-1512 and head 1-472. The range map is complete. The visible head change adds an internal init parameter `environment: [String: String]?` (head 80-81, 166-167, 173). It is documented as the environment this Mac's parts start from via `partEnvironment`; nil means this process's own environment at each start. Public callers use the convenience init (head 159-161), so the default stays nil and production behavior is unchanged unless another internal caller supplies an environment.

Head lines 1301-1302, 1428-1429 and 1448-1463 were not supplied. They likely include the `partEnvironment` implementation and how `process.environment` is set in supervise; base supervise sets no environment (base 1419-1426). Base 1127-1128 (now head 1131-1133) changes how `approvalSetAside` is recorded for `.serveLocally`. Base 1296 is a comment change. I could not see the new text of either change.

Security questions for integration:
(1) Does `partEnvironment` filter or override security-relevant variables passed to child parts? Examples are DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE / _SSD_TTL_SECONDS / _DISK_GB (T-041) and the coordinator URL or token settings (A-008, TB-011). Could it drop the operator's kill switch, or inject values not controlled by the operator?
(2) Does the approvalSetAside change preserve the binding to the worker digest (`decided.worker`)? Could it let a set-aside or expired cluster approval be reused after an update (T-053, T-054)? Note the supervise guard at base 1325-1332 and 1378-1388 that stops or removes ended approvals.
(3) Confirm `environment` is only injectable by tests or internal composition, not by the link command channel from a paired peer.

No regression is evidenced in the visible source. Coverage of the head hunks above is missing, so this is not a clearance.
